(a) graph databases can be a powerful tool for analyzing IPFLOW data and (b) IPFLOW data can serve as a useful test bed for graph database research and development.
graph database systems are a promising technology for cyber traffic analysis.

massive scale cyber traffic analysis requires: (1) a hybrid graph-relational system, (2) efficient query processing for complex graph patterns, (3) efficient storage of large, sparse graphs, and (4) a scalable graph database system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of graph database systems that can support massive-scale cyber traffic analysis.
the development of a new generation of database management systems that are capable of supporting massive-scale, graph-oriented cyber traffic analysis.
the design of a new generation of graph database systems that can scale to the massive graphs that arise in cyber traffic analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problem of massive scale cyber traffic analysis is a driver for new research in graph database technology.
IPFLOW analytics are a compelling use case for graph databases, and graph database technology will be an essential component of future cybersecurity systems.
the problem domain is sufficiently interesting, and the technology is sufficiently immature, to justify significant research investment in graph databases for cyber traffic analysis.

the graph-structured IPFLOWS data is an ideal testbed for graph database research, and that we have made a good start on this research agenda.
the IPFLOW graph is a new driver for research in graph databases, with implications for both theory and practice.
we have identified a class of problems that are not well supported in current systems and that are likely to benefit from the development of hybrid graph-relational systems.

graph databases have an opportunity to make a significant impact on cyber security by enabling massive scale cyber traffic analysis.
graph database systems can play a key role in the analysis of large-scale, complex cyber data.
